topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture, recaps histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation, oncogenes, genetic instability, and hereditary cancer predispositions.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and experimental identification of transforming genes
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the historical study of tumor viruses revealed that oncogenes originate from cellular genes and outline the laboratory assays used to test cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classifications and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: They define the functional classifications of cancer-associated genes and illustrate their genetic behaviors and dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms using cell cycle regulators such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the distinctions between sequence instability and chromosomal instability and explore the specific DNA repair, replication, and mitotic segregation defects that generate them.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor development and describe how inherited germline mutations in caretaker and gatekeeper genes accelerate cancer progression and shape tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes, offers a reading recommendation, and previews the next lecture on cancer hallmarks.
